newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl hopes Yugoslav republics can join EU.
newsitem.headline: Kohl hopes Yugoslav republics can join EU.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday he hoped the republics of former Yugoslavia could become members of the European Union sometime early in the next century.
He also said at a news conference he hoped that Serbia would become a peaceful democracy soon.

"For us Germans, it's clear that we would like the republics that emerged from former Yugoslavia to become members of the European Union in a period in the initial part of the next century, not at the end of the next century," he said.
"It's being discussed openly (now) whether Slovenia shold be in the first wave of expansion."

Germany, which championed the independence bids by Slovenia and Croatia in 1991, has long argued that the European Union should take in many of the east European states if they qualify for membership.

Speaking after breaking ground for the new chancellery to be ready when the government moves from Bonn in 1999, he said Brussels would by that time already be negotiating entry with the first east European states due to join.
"Berlin will be at the centre of the future Europe, not on its edge," he said.
